proposals.label: Open-weight baseline (no SERV)

analysis.what_went_wrong: The model is systematically under-predicting PM2.5 levels across most stations, as indicated by the negative mean error (-2.23 ug/m3). Several stations (e.g., ME2, WAB, GN0) show particularly large under-predictions. The sample errors confirm this trend.
analysis.pattern_discovered: The under-prediction is consistent across stations, suggesting a global bias in the model. Stations with higher actual PM2.5 values tend to have larger absolute errors, indicating the model may not be capturing the full impact of high PM2.5 conditions. The negative coefficients for humidity, wind, and precipitation are likely contributing to the under-prediction, as they reduce the predicted value when these factors are at their baseline (50% humidity, 5 m/s wind, 0 precipitation).
analysis.change_made: I propose a small increase to the bias term and a slight increase to the scale of the PM2.5 model. I will also slightly reduce the negative impact of humidity, wind, and precipitation by making their coefficients less negative.
analysis.why_it_should_help: Increasing the bias will directly address the systematic under-prediction. Increasing the scale will amplify the effect of the PM2.5 model, potentially capturing higher PM2.5 values more accurately. Reducing the negative impact of humidity, wind, and precipitation will prevent these factors from overly suppressing the prediction. These are conservative changes designed to nudge the model towards better accuracy without risking over-correction.
